articles.description:
I maintain a small Chrome extension that translates text with Chrome's built-in AI. It doesn't have many users, but I update it now and then, and every update meant the same routine: bump the version, write the changelog, build, zip, sign in to the store dashboard, upload and submit. None of it was hard. It was just easy to get wrong, like the time I forgot the version number and the store refused the upload.
Most guides for automating this put a long-lived credential in your CI secrets, either a service account key or an OAuth refresh token. That works, but it means a key that never expires sits next to your code. If it leaks, anyone can publish as you.
I wanted the automation without a key to lose.

1. Let the commits decide the version. I write commit messages in the Conventional Commit…

articles.author: Tanu Priya
articles.description:
Imagine a payment succeeds, but your system records a related database event before the payment itself. The payment service logs the transaction at 10:00:00.120, while the database records the event at 10:00:00.095.
When you inspect the logs, it looks as though the database event happened first. But what if the application logic is correct and the real problem is that the two servers disagree about the current time?
This is one of the more frustrating problems in distributed systems. Timestamps look like reliable facts, yet they can tell a misleading story when events happen across multiple machines.
Developers use timestamps to track transactions, process messages, expire sessions, and resolve database conflicts. Understanding where these timestamps fail is essential when building systems…
articles.title: Why Is Keeping Time Correctly So Difficult for Distributed Systems?

Linked to the long-running MALFEX supply chain campaign, the package exemplifies ongoing risks in package registry security.

CVE-2026-87799 Versus CVE-2026-85185: Symlink Replay and Unvalidated Subvolume Paths Compared



  
  
  Two ways to escape the same volume


CVE-2026-87799 and CVE-2026-85185 both let LXD act outside the storage volume it was asked to write to. They differ in mechanism, in the code that fails, and in which hosts they reach.
This is CWE-59, rated 9.9. LXD receives an instance or custom volume through migration and delegates the replay to rsync or to btrfs receive. Both tools use path-based system calls and neither refuses to traverse a symlink planted earlier in the same stream. Later entries travel through the link and are written as root outside the destination volume.
This is CWE-22, rated 9.6. The btrfs storage driver reads a subvolume path field from attacker-supplied backup or migrat…

Maintainers usually find out a dependency is dead when something breaks. Every small business runs on WhatsApp. Orders, questions, follow-ups — it all happens there.
But answering the same questions 50 times a day? That's not a business, that's a treadmill.
So I built WhatsAppKit — 4 production-ready n8n workflows that turn WhatsApp into your hardest-working employee.
Customer messages on WhatsApp — sees your menu — places an order by name or number — gets confirmation. Everything logged to Google Sheets, you get an instant alert. No app to install, no website needed.
Every inquiry gets scored 1-10 by AI (Ollama locally, or OpenAI). Hot leads (7+) ping you immediately with the details. Cold ones get logged quietly. You stop chasing, start closing.
Answers from YOUR knowledge base — in English and Roman Urdu. It can't hallucinate because it can only answer from what you taught it. Unmatched questions get forwarded to you.
Send personalized WhatsApp messages to customers who said yes. Template-based (Meta-compliant), logged, respectful. No spam — consent is checked before every send.
WhatsApp Cloud API (free tier: 1,000 conversations/month) via a free Meta developer app
n8n self-hosted (free)
Ollama for local AI (free) or OpenAI
Google Sheets as the database
Every workflow has a CONFIG node (all keys in one place) and a setup sticky in Roman Urdu + English.
You need your own Meta app + WhatsApp Cloud API — setup steps included, free tier is generous
n8n needs a public HTTPS URL for Meta webhooks (localhost won't work)
Dashboard tokens expire in 24h — the guide shows how to get a permanent System User token
WhatsAppKit — $49 one-time, commercial license included:
https://mohsina91.gumroad.com/l/ttxqw
Launch code WHATSAPP10 takes $10 off.
This is the companion to my AgentKit (5 Telegram AI agents) — same local-first philosophy, different battlefield.
